items.stem: Define the term 'price elasticity of demand (PED)'.
items.answer: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why knowledge of price elasticity of demand is useful when setting prices.
items.answer: It shows how quantity and revenue will respond: if demand is inelastic a price rise increases revenue; if elastic, a price cut may increase revenue.
items.markingKey: 1 mark predicts quantity/revenue response; 1 mark applied to pricing decision. [2]

items.stem: Explain two limitations of using elasticity estimates for marketing decisions.
items.answer: They are based on past data and conditions change; other factors (competitors' prices, incomes, tastes) do not stay constant; estimates may only be valid for small price changes.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark limitation, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Based in Lisbon, Tejo Mobility SA (public limited company) assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union. The business has around 600 employees. Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. Explain why the price elasticity of demand for Tejo Mobility's electric scooters and e-bikes might change over time.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tejo Mobility: PED depends on substitutes, brand loyalty, necessity and share of income; new competitors create closer substitutes; branding and quality can reduce elasticity; changes in income alter price sensitivity.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: PED depends on substitutes, brand loyalty, necessity and share of income. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Tejo Mobility: vehicle manufacturing, about 600 employees, public limited company in Portugal; battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Tejo Mobility, e.g. new competitors create closer substitutes; branding and quality can reduce elasticity; changes in income alter price sensitivity. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Andes Textil SA is a family-owned private company based in Lima, Peru. It makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan and employs about 320 people. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Explain why the price elasticity of demand for Andes Textil's alpaca knitwear might change over time.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andes Textil: PED depends on substitutes, brand loyalty, necessity and share of income; new competitors create closer substitutes; branding and quality can reduce elasticity; changes in income alter price sensitivity.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: PED depends on substitutes, brand loyalty, necessity and share of income. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Andes Textil: textile manufacturing, about 320 employees, family-owned private company in Peru; the founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Andes Textil, e.g. new competitors create closer substitutes; branding and quality can reduce elasticity; changes in income alter price sensitivity. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd, a private limited company in Ghana with about 450 employees, buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. Discuss the usefulness of elasticity of demand calculations for Gold Coast Cocoa.
items.answer: For: help forecast effects of price and promotion; guide pricing strategy; help plan for the business cycle. Against: estimates rely on past data; other things do not stay equal; hard to measure accurately. Judgement: the decision for Gold Coast Cocoa depends mainly on the quality of its market data, and also on how stable its market is.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Gold Coast Cocoa: confectionery, about 450 employees, private limited company in Ghana; world cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. help forecast effects of price and promotion; guide pricing strategy; help plan for the business cycle; arguments against, e.g. estimates rely on past data; other things do not stay equal; hard to measure accurately. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the quality of its market data; how stable its market is; how decisions also use qualitative judgement. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Gold Coast Cocoa, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Nusantara Apparel Tbk is a public limited company based in Jakarta, Indonesia. It makes sportswear under contract for global brands and employs about 4,000 people. A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Using the case and your own knowledge, evaluate whether Nusantara Apparel should raise the price of its sportswear by 10%.
items.answer: For: higher revenue if demand is price inelastic; higher margins; premium image. Against: sales fall sharply if demand is elastic; competitors may not follow; brand loyalty could suffer. Judgement: the decision for Nusantara Apparel depends mainly on the estimated price elasticity, and also on competitors' likely reaction.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Nusantara Apparel: clothing manufacturing, about 4,000 employees, public limited company in Indonesia; a global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours). AO3 Analysis [5]: arguments for, e.g. higher revenue if demand is price inelastic; higher margins; premium image; arguments against, e.g. sales fall sharply if demand is elastic; competitors may not follow; brand loyalty could suffer. AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the estimated price elasticity; competitors' likely reaction; its objectives (market share or profit). Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Nusantara Apparel, not a generic one. [16]

items.stem: Its car-maker customers are switching rapidly to electric vehicles. Deccan Auto Components Ltd, a public limited company in India with about 2,200 employees, supplies brakes and steering parts to car manufacturers. Explain one advantage to Deccan Auto of making demand for its brake and steering components less price elastic through branding.
items.answer: Able to raise prices without losing many customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. able to raise prices without losing many customers; higher revenue and margins; less vulnerable to price competition. 1 mark: explained in the context of Deccan Auto (automotive components). [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business would prefer the demand for its product to be price inelastic.
items.answer: It can raise prices with only a small loss of sales, so revenue and margins rise; it is less vulnerable to rivals' price cuts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark pricing power; 1 mark effect on revenue/profit. [2]

items.stem: Average real incomes in Thailand changed by +4% last year. Monthly sales of one of Siam Ready Meals' product lines changed from 10,000 to 11,000 units, with prices unchanged. Calculate the income elasticity of demand.
items.answer: YED = 2.5

items.stem: Desert Bloom Hotels plc is a public limited company based in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. It operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels and employs about 3,100 people. Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Explain how Desert Bloom could use estimates of price and income elasticity of demand to plan its marketing, and judge which point is most important for Desert Bloom.
items.answer: Points to develop for Desert Bloom: PED shows revenue response to price changes; YED shows how demand changes over the business cycle; set prices to maximise revenue or profit; plan production and promotion for forecast demand.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: PED shows revenue response to price changes. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Desert Bloom: hospitality, about 3,100 employees, public limited company in the United Arab Emirates; occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Desert Bloom, e.g. YED shows how demand changes over the business cycle; set prices to maximise revenue or profit; plan production and promotion for forecast demand. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Han River Games Co. is a private limited company based in Seoul, South Korea. It develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases and employs about 340 people. One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. (a) Define 'promotional elasticity of demand'. (b) Explain one advantage to Han River Games of making demand for its mobile games less price elastic through branding.
items.answer: (a) The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in promotional (advertising) spending: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in promotional spending. (b) Able to raise prices without losing many customers.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (able to raise prices without losing many customers; higher revenue and margins; less vulnerable to price competition), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Han River Games [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'sales forecasting'.
items.answer: Predicting future sales volume or value, using quantitative methods (e.g. moving averages) and/or qualitative methods (e.g. expert opinion).
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, predicting future sales volume or value, using quantitative methods (e.g. moving averages) and/or qualitative methods (e.g. expert opinion). 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business might use qualitative forecasting methods as well as moving averages.
items.answer: Moving averages only project the past; expert opinion or the Delphi method can allow for new products, competitors or economic shocks that the data do not show.
items.markingKey: 1 mark limitation of quantitative methods; 1 mark benefit of qualitative. [2]

items.stem: Explain how accurate sales forecasts help the operations department.
items.answer: They allow capacity, staffing and inventory to be planned, avoiding shortages or excess stock.
items.markingKey: 1 mark planning; 1 mark consequence. [2]

items.stem: Many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities. Lanka Tea Estates plc, a public limited company in Sri Lanka with about 5,000 employees, grows, processes and packs tea on its own estates. Explain how more accurate sales forecasts could improve the performance of Lanka Tea.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lanka Tea: sales forecasting predicts future demand; better capacity and workforce planning; lower inventory holding and fewer stock-outs; more accurate cash-flow forecasts and budgets.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: sales forecasting predicts future demand. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Lanka Tea: agriculture and food, about 5,000 employees, public limited company in Sri Lanka; many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Lanka Tea, e.g. better capacity and workforce planning; lower inventory holding and fewer stock-outs; more accurate cash-flow forecasts and budgets. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: forecasts extrapolate past trends; changes in the economy and incomes; competitors' actions; changes in consumer tastes and random events.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: forecasts extrapolate past trends. items.stem: Iberia Moda SA is a public limited company based in Madrid, Spain. It runs 180 fast-fashion clothing stores and an online shop and employs about 6,000 people. Online sales are growing quickly while sales in its high-street stores are falling. Evaluate the usefulness of quantitative sales forecasting methods to Iberia Moda.
items.answer: For: objective and based on data; show trend and seasonal patterns; help plan production and cash. Against: assume the past continues; cannot predict shocks; new products have no data. Judgement: the decision for Iberia Moda depends mainly on how stable its market is, and also on whether qualitative methods are also used.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. items.stem: Based in Cairo, Nile Pharma plc (public limited company) manufactures generic medicines for hospitals and pharmacies in Africa and the Middle East. The business has around 1,800 employees. Most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars. Explain one advantage to Nile Pharma of using moving averages to forecast sales of its generic medicines.
items.answer: Identifies the trend and seasonal pattern.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. identifies the trend and seasonal pattern; based on objective data; helps plan inventory and staffing. 1 mark: explained in the context of Nile Pharma (pharmaceuticals). [2]

items.stem: Explain what is meant by random variation in sales data and why it makes forecasting difficult.
items.answer: Random variations are unpredictable changes (e.g. weather, strikes) not explained by trend or season; they cannot be forecast, so forecasts may be inaccurate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark meaning; 1 mark difficulty. [2]

items.stem: Quarterly sales (thousand units) of Lanka Tea Estates plc were — Y1 Q1: 808; Y1 Q2: 832; Y1 Q3: 798; Y1 Q4: 782; Y2 Q1: 824; Y2 Q2: 850; Y2 Q3: 812; Y2 Q4: 796; Y3 Q1: 840; Y3 Q2: 866; Y3 Q3: 832; Y3 Q4: 816. Calculate the four-quarter centred moving average (trend) for Y2 Q3.
items.answer: Trend = 822.5
items.markingKey: Four-quarter totals: 3282 and 3298 [1]; centred total = 6580 [1]; trend = 6580/8 = 822.5 [1]. [3]

items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. (a) Define 'extrapolation'. (b) Explain one advantage to Pearl Logistics of using moving averages to forecast sales of its freight and warehousing services.
items.answer: (a) Extending a trend line beyond the existing data to forecast future values. (b) Identifies the trend and seasonal pattern.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (identifies the trend and seasonal pattern; based on objective data; helps plan inventory and staffing), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Pearl Logistics [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'correlation'.
items.answer: A statistical measure of the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables, e.g. advertising spending and sales.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, a statistical measure of the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables, e.g. advertising spending and sales. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why strong correlation between two variables does not prove that one causes the other.
items.answer: Both may be influenced by a third factor, the relationship may be coincidental, or causation may run the other way.
items.markingKey: 1 mark third factor/coincidence; 1 mark example or reverse causation. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a business could use correlation to plan its advertising budget.
items.answer: If sales and advertising spending are strongly positively correlated, a line of best fit can estimate the sales likely from different budgets, helping to choose the spending level.
items.markingKey: 1 mark identifies relationship; 1 mark use for forecasting/budgeting. [2]

items.stem: Based in Kuala Lumpur, BatikPay Sdn Bhd (private limited company) runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops. The business has around 210 employees. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. Explain why a strong correlation between BatikPay's social media spending and its sales might be misleading.
items.answer: Points to develop for BatikPay: correlation does not prove causation; sales may rise for other reasons (season, incomes); reverse causation: higher sales fund more spending; small samples can give misleading results.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: correlation does not prove causation. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (BatikPay: financial technology, about 210 employees, private limited company in Malaysia; the central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for BatikPay, e.g. sales may rise for other reasons (season, incomes); reverse causation: higher sales fund more spending; small samples can give misleading results. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

Many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities. Explain how Lanka Tea could use correlation analysis to improve its marketing decisions.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lanka Tea: correlation measures the relationship between variables; identifies factors linked to sales of packaged tea; line of best fit forecasts sales; must test whether the link is causal before acting.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: correlation measures the relationship between variables. Maple Learning Inc., a private limited company in Canada with about 260 employees, runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students. Evaluate the usefulness of correlation analysis for Maple Learning's marketing planning.
items.answer: For: identifies relationships; supports forecasts; objective evidence. Against: not proof of causation; relationships change; quality of data. Judgement: the decision for Maple Learning depends mainly on the strength of the correlation, and also on whether a causal mechanism is plausible.

items.stem: A correlation coefficient of −0.9 between price and sales indicates
items.answer: a strong negative relationship
items.markingKey: a strong negative relationship. Values close to −1 show a strong inverse relationship.

items.stem: Based in Hanoi, Mekong Furniture JSC (joint stock company) makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe. The business has around 1,200 employees. A major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six. Explain one disadvantage to Mekong Furniture of using correlation analysis to decide its advertising budget.
items.answer: Correlation is not causation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. correlation is not causation; relationship may change; other factors are ignored. 1 mark: explained in the context of Mekong Furniture (furniture manufacturing). [2]

items.stem: Lanka Tea Estates plc plotted monthly sales (S, thousand units) against advertising spending (A, $000). The line of best fit is S = 50 + 3A, and the correlation coefficient is 0.45. Calculate forecast sales when advertising is $25,000 and the extra sales from increasing advertising by $5,000. Comment on the strength of the correlation.
items.answer: 125 thousand units; +15 thousand
items.markingKey: S = 50 + 3 × 25 = 125 thousand [1]; extra = 3 × 5 = 15 thousand units [1]; r = 0.45 is weak to moderate positive, so the forecast is not very reliable [1]. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'big data'.
items.answer: Extremely large and fast-growing sets of data, e.g. from online transactions, social media and sensors, that can be analysed by computers to reveal patterns and trends.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, extremely large and fast-growing sets of data, e.g. from online transactions, social media and sensors, that can be analysed by computers to reveal patterns and trends. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Which is the best example of a business using big data?
options: A shop owner asking ten customers their opinion
A manager reading last year's annual report
An online retailer recommending products based on millions of customers' browsing histories
items.answer: An online retailer recommending products based on millions of customers' browsing histories
items.markingKey: An online retailer recommending products based on millions of customers' browsing histories. Big data involves analysing very large, fast-changing data sets.

items.stem: Explain how big data could help a retailer target its promotions more effectively.
items.answer: Analysis of purchase and browsing data identifies segments and individual preferences, so offers can be personalised and sent at the right time, raising conversion rates.
items.markingKey: 1 mark analysis of customer data; 1 mark more targeted/personalised promotion. [2]

items.answer: 1.5%; $8.33 per customer

items.stem: If demand for a product is price inelastic, a price rise will
items.answer: increase total revenue
items.markingKey: increase total revenue. With |PED| < 1 the % fall in quantity is smaller than the % rise in price.

items.stem: Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd is a private limited company based in Bangkok, Thailand. It produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores and employs about 1,100 people. Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. Discuss the usefulness of elasticity of demand calculations for Siam Ready Meals.
items.answer: For: help forecast effects of price and promotion; guide pricing strategy; help plan for the business cycle. Against: estimates rely on past data; other things do not stay equal; hard to measure accurately. Judgement: the decision for Siam Ready Meals depends mainly on the quality of its market data, and also on how stable its market is.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Siam Ready Meals: food manufacturing, about 1,100 employees, private limited company in Thailand; its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. help forecast effects of price and promotion; guide pricing strategy; help plan for the business cycle; arguments against, e.g. estimates rely on past data; other things do not stay equal; hard to measure accurately. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the quality of its market data; how stable its market is; how decisions also use qualitative judgement. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Siam Ready Meals, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Why is a four-quarter moving average "centred"?
options: To calculate the seasonal variation directly
Because the average of four quarters falls between two quarters, so two averages are averaged to line up with a quarter
Because it uses only odd numbers of data
items.answer: Because the average of four quarters falls between two quarters, so two averages are averaged to line up with a quarter
items.markingKey: Because the average of four quarters falls between two quarters, so two averages are averaged to line up with a quarter. An even-period moving average must be centred to match a specific period.

items.stem: IslaConnect Inc. is a private limited company based in Manila, the Philippines. items.answer: For: past relationship suggests more sales; competitors may be advertising more; line of best fit predicts gains. items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'price elasticity of demand (PED)'?
options: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in promotional (advertising) spending: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in promotional spending.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price.
Extremely large and fast-growing sets of data, e.g. from online transactions, social media and sensors, that can be analysed by computers to reveal patterns and trends.
A graph plotting pairs of values of two variables, used to see whether they are correlated and to draw a line of best fit.
items.answer: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price.
items.markingKey: price elasticity of demand (PED): The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price.

Judgement: the decision for Desert Bloom depends mainly on the estimated price elasticity, and also on competitors' likely reaction.

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'moving average'?

Using software to search large data sets for patterns and relationships, e.g. which products customers buy together.
An average of a fixed number of consecutive data values, recalculated each period, used to smooth out fluctuations and reveal the trend.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price.
items.answer: An average of a fixed number of consecutive data values, recalculated each period, used to smooth out fluctuations and reveal the trend.
